'''Christopher Derek Hacon''' (born 14 February 1970) is a mathematician with British, Italian and US nationalities.<ref>As Hacon states in his [https://www.math.utah.edu/~hacon/cv.pdf Curriculum Vitae]</ref>  He is currently distinguished professor of mathematics at the [[University of Utah]] where he holds a Presidential Endowed Chair. His research interests include [[algebraic geometry]].

Hacon was born in [[Manchester]], but grew up in Italy where he studied at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore]] and received a degree in mathematics at the [[University of Pisa]] in 1992. He received his doctorate from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1998, under supervision of [[Robert Lazarsfeld]].

==Awards and honors==
In 2007, he was awarded a Clay Research Award for his work, joint with [[James McKernan]], on "the birational geometry of algebraic varieties in dimension greater than three, in particular, for [an] inductive proof of the existence of flips."
<ref>{{cite web|title=Clay Research Awards|url=https://www.claymath.org/research|publisher=[[Clay Mathematics Institute]]}}</ref>

In 2009, he was awarded the [[Cole Prize]] for outstanding contribution to algebra, along with McKernan.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200904/rtx090400494p.pdf|
title=2009 Cole Prize in Algebra}}</ref>

He was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] 2010 in [[Hyderabad]], on the topic of "''Algebraic Geometry.''"<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=14 August 2013|archive-date=8 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2011, he was awarded the [[Feltrinelli Prize|Antonio Feltrinelli Prize]] in Mathematics, Mechanics and Applications by Italy's prestigious [[Accademia dei Lincei|Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://maa.org/news/math-news/utah-mathematician-awarded-italys-top-scientific-prize|title=Utah Mathematician Awarded Italy's Top Scientific Prize|date=June 23, 2011 |publisher=Mathematical Association of America|access-date=2024-04-10}}</ref>

In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 19 January 2013.</ref>

In 2012, he became a [[Simons Investigator]].<ref>[https://www.simonsfoundation.org/mathematics-physical-sciences/simons-investigators/simons-investigators-awardees/ Simons Investigators Awardees], The Simons Foundation</ref>

In 2015, he won the American Mathematical Society Moore Prize.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/ams-prizes/moore-prize AMS Moore Prize], retrieved 1 December 2015.</ref>

In 2017, he was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.<ref>[https://www.amacad.org/content/members/newFellows.aspx?s=a 2017 Fellows of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences], retrieved 1 December 2017.</ref>

In 2017, he won the 2018 [[Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics]] (with [[James McKernan]]).<ref>[https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/3/L3817 Breakthrough Prize], retrieved 12 April 2017.</ref>

In 2018, he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].

In 2019, he was elected to the [[Royal Society]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Distinguished scientists elected as Fellows and Foreign Members of the Royal Society {{!}} Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2019/04/royal-society-announces-2019-fellows/ |website=royalsociety.org |access-date=18 April 2019 |language=en-gb}}</ref>
